entries.summary: Weekend assessment retains bearish elevated-downside outlook for Nov 23-25. Reuters Friday closing Nasdaq -5.28%, SOX approximately -11%, and Nvidia approximately -14% confirm severe semiconductor-led selling. QQQ -5.67% reported at 16:00 ET by StockTitan. New review adds secondary reported decliners-to-advancers about 4:1, and FT's report that Nasdaq 100 entered bear-market territory, but these reinforce rather than materially change the prior bearish path. Open Watch 174 events, no new curated catalyst.

editorial.marketOverview: Friday's final U.S. session showed extreme AI and semiconductor selling: Reuters reported Nasdaq -5.28% and SOX roughly -11%, while a timestamped secondary close reported QQQ -5.67% and Nvidia -14.01%. Financial Times described Nasdaq 100 in bear-market territory. These are closing-day reports, not new Saturday trading.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the 20:25 ET assessment, there is no new trading session or newly curated Open Watch event. Independent reporting adds an approximate four-to-one negative breadth ratio and confirms the depth of Nasdaq 100's drawdown, reinforcing the existing bearish baseline without establishing a new change in the expected path.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Sector leadership and breadth deterioration plus sharply elevated volatility imply severe risk aversion. Reuters' 10Y yield near 4.93% after a 12bp decline suggests safe-haven demand, but the available 2Y figure is older and cannot support a synchronized current curve. Earlier 4.94% minus 4.65% equals 29bp, not 0.29bp. Oil maturity mismatch and absent direct FedWatch limit macro precision. No headline is assigned definitive causal responsibility.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23 may bring continued downside pressure or a violent oversold bounce. Tuesday's chip and AI infrastructure earnings test whether semiconductor leadership can stabilize. Wednesday's GDP/PCE-related releases and Fed Beige Book add event-driven rate and risk-premium uncertainty. Downside continuation remains the baseline until breadth and volatility corroborate sustained QQQ/chip recovery.
editorial.bullCase: Sharp capitulation-like price action may invite short covering, and lower yields could provide some support. A credible bullish reversal needs QQQ and SOX/SMH strengthening together, breadth turning more positive and VIX/VXN declining through Tuesday, not merely a one-hour bounce.
editorial.bearCase: The combination of a greater-than-5% Nasdaq decline, roughly 11% semiconductor drop, heavy Nvidia selling, approximately four decliners per advancer and VIX in the high 30s signals persistent downside fragility. Weak Tuesday AI-hardware guidance would add further pressure.
editorial.watchNext: Confirm Monday opening and close across QQQ/SOX/SMH, VXN/VIX, breadth and paired 10Y/2Y; check direct FedWatch and oil futures maturities; monitor Monday HPE/Zoom, Tuesday Analog Devices/Dell and Wednesday macro releases. Recheck curated Open Watch events before attributing any new catalyst.
